title: Company-wide policies and processes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and operational processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, managers, and approvers.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and contingent workers.
- Covers corporate systems (SSO, GSuite/Okta), production and non-production cloud accounts, procurement of services/hardware, and business travel.
- Does not replace team-specific runbooks or compliance evidence; where conflicts exist, this doc points to the authoritative team page.

1) Access and permissions

Summary
- Access to systems is granted on the principle of least privilege and must have a documented business justification. All identity management is centralized through Okta (primary SSO) and SCIM-provisioned groups where possible.

Roles and responsibilities
- Requester: employee or manager who initiates access request.
- Manager: approves role assignment and attests ongoing need during quarterly access reviews.
- IAM Owner (Security & Compliance): configures role definitions and approves exceptions.
- System Owner: maintains audit logs and verifies users in their system.

Standard access flow (1–3 business days)
1. Submit request via Access Request form (Confluence template: "access-request-template").
2. Manager approves in the access system and notes the business justification.
3. IAM Owner validates and provisions via Okta/SCIM or sends to system owner for manual provisioning.

Temporary and emergency access
- Temporary elevated access (jumpboxes, admin keys) should be requested with an explicit expiry (max 72 hours) and logged in the privileged access tracker (sheet link in templates).
- Emergency access follows the incident process (see oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process) and must be reviewed post-event.

Quarterly review
- Managers receive a quarterly access report and must attest within 10 business days. Non-attested accounts are flagged for removal.

2) Change management

Goal
- Ensure changes to production services, infra-as-code, and platform configurations are authorized, tested, and observable with rollback plans.

Change categories and approvals
- Standard change: routine, low-risk (e.g., non-prod config updates) — self-service via PR and automated tests. Approver: team lead.
- Significant change: code or infra changes affecting production behavior (latency, correctness) — requires staging tests and a peer review plus SRE sign-off.
- Major change: architectural or cross-team changes (network, major schema migration) — requires formal change request, impact analysis, and CTO or Head of Eng approval.

Required artifacts for Significant/Major changes
- Change request describing impact, rollback plan, monitoring queries, and blast radius table.
- Test plan and results (perf/regression).
- Deployment window and oncall coverage.

Change window and blackout periods
- Standard deployment window: 09:00–18:00 local (Mon–Fri) unless otherwise authorized.
- Blackout periods: company-wide (e.g., major conferences, fiscal close weeks) where production-impacting changes are disallowed.

Post-deploy verification
1. Run smoke tests and SLO checks (latency P50/P95, error-rate).
2. If metrics exceed thresholds in the monitoring runbook, initiate rollback per rollback playbook.

3) Data management

Data classification
- Public: intended for all external audiences.
- Internal: Redwood-internal, permissible to share with partners under NDA.
- Confidential: contains PII, customer data, or sensitive business metrics.

Storage and access controls
- Confidential data must be stored in encrypted services (KMS-backed). Access requires justification and must be provisioned with the least privilege.
- Backups for production data must follow the backup policy on eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking (daily backups, 30-day retention for non-sensitive, longer per contract).

Retention and disposal
- Retention periods are defined per data class and business need. Example: logs (90 days default), support transcripts (2 years), customer data (per contract).
- Secure deletion checklist: archive identifiers, revoke access, securely wipe storage, update inventory.

Data sharing and vendor transfers
- Transfers to third parties require Data Processing Agreements (DPA) reviewed by Finance & Legal. Data transfers outside allowed regions require explicit approval by Security & Legal.

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals (table)
| Amount (USD) | Approval required | Typical approver | Procurement process |
|--------------|-------------------|------------------|--------------------|
| <= 2,500     | Manager           | Hiring manager / team lead | P-card or self-service purchase; retain receipts |
| 2,500–25,000 | Director          | Budget owner / Director | Purchase Order (PO) requested via Procurement portal; vendor onboarding |
| > 25,000     | VP / Finance Lead | VP / Finance Lead | Formal procurement, multi-vendor bids, legal review required |

Expense policy highlights
- Employees should submit expense reports within 10 business days of travel/expense.
- Per diem and allowable categories are described in the travel section and expense templates. Unapproved or non-compliant expenses may be denied.

Procurement process steps (typical)
1. Create a PR with business justification and budget code.
2. Procurement reviews vendor compliance, insurance, and SLA (if applicable).
3. Finance approves PO and issues payment terms.
4. Receive goods/services and confirm acceptance in the procurement system.

5) Vendor management

Vendor onboarding checklist
- Complete vendor profile in procurement system.
- Validate vendor insurance, SOC reports (if handling data), and security questionnaire.
- Execute contracts (MSA/SOW) with Finance & Legal.

Vendor risk tiers
- Low: commodity services (office supplies). Minimal oversight.
- Medium: SaaS with limited data (bug trackers). Require security questionnaire and contract.
- High: services processing customer data or impact production (model hosting, data labeling). Require SOC2/ISO evidence, DPA, security architecture review, and periodic audits.

Contract lifecycle and renewals
- IT & Procurement own contract repository. Renewal notices are sent 90/60/30 days before expiration. High-risk vendor renewal requires a security re-review.

6) Travel policies

Pre-approval and booking
- All business travel must be pre-approved using the Travel Request template (Confluence template: "travel-request-template").
- Preferred suppliers and negotiated rates must be used when available.

Allowable expenses and per diem
- Employees are reimbursed for reasonable airfare (economy/upgrade rules documented in template), lodging, ground transport, and meals. Per diem values by country are provided in the travel template. Receipts required for amounts > $25.

Travel safety and emergency communication
- Travelers must register trips in the company travel tracker and share itinerary with their manager and people-ops. In emergencies contact the oncall emergency number; People Ops will coordinate assistance and insurance claims.

7) Internal templates and process artifacts

Canonical templates (Confluence)
- access-request-template (Access requests)
- change-request-template (Change Management)
- procurement-requisition-template (Procurement/PO)
- travel-request-template (Travel approval)
- vendor-onboarding-checklist (Vendor management)
- expense-report-template (Expense submission)

How to use templates
1. Create a new page from the template. Fill required fields (owner, justification, budget code, dates).
2. Link supporting artifacts (test results, security signoffs).
3. Assign reviewers and approvers according to the policy.

Enforcement, exceptions, and escalation
- Exceptions to any policy must be documented and approved by the relevant owner_team and recorded in the Exceptions register.
- Violations discovered during audits will be remediated per the remediation playbook; repeat violations escalate to HR or Legal as appropriate.

Appendix: quick checklists and links
- Access request: include user, systems, justification, expected duration.
- Change request: include rollback plan, monitoring queries, runbook links.
- Procurement: include budget code, vendor contact, contract owner.

Related pages and references
- eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking: cloud account standards and backup policy.
- security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth: RBAC standard and SSO configuration.
- finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process: contract templates and DPA guidance.

Contact and ownership
- Document owner: People Ops (owner_team). For questions or to request an exception, contact people-ops@redwood-inference.example.
